author: Scott Westerfeld
keyCast: Joey King, Keith Powers, Chase Stokes, Laverne Cox
notes: This film adapts the first book in Scott Westerfeld's popular dystopian YA series, set in a future where everyone undergoes extreme cosmetic surgery at age 16 to become 'Pretties'. The story follows Tally Youngblood as she grapples with this enforced conformity. Directed by McG, the project has been in development for some time but finally completed filming in late 2025, with Joey King in the lead role she has championed for years. Fans of the early 2000s YA dystopian boom will be eager to see this world come to life. Reading the book first is a good idea to grasp the world's unique slang and social structure, which might be streamlined in the film.

author: Hugh Howey
keyCast: Rebecca Ferguson, Tim Robbins, Common, Harriet Walter
notes: The second season of the hit sci-fi series continues the story from Hugh Howey's 'Wool' trilogy, exploring the mysteries of a massive underground silo that houses the last remnants of humanity. Following the explosive cliffhanger of Season 1, this season is expected to delve deeper into the silo's history and the truth of the outside world. Production was completed in early 2026, and the show is one of Apple TV+'s flagship properties, known for its incredible production design and tense atmosphere. While the first season can be enjoyed on its own, reading the 'Wool' omnibus is highly recommended for those who can't stand the wait, as it provides a complete and satisfying narrative arc.

author: Simon Stålenhag
keyCast: Millie Bobby Brown, Chris Pratt, Ke Huy Quan, Stanley Tucci, Giancarlo Esposito
notes: Based on the acclaimed illustrated narrative book by Simon Stålenhag, this film is a major sci-fi event from directors Joe and Anthony Russo. The story follows a teenage girl (Brown) and her small yellow robot as they travel across a retro-futuristic 1990s American West littered with the ruins of giant battle drones. With a massive budget, an all-star cast, and the creative team behind 'Avengers: Endgame', this is one of Netflix's biggest bets for the year. The source material is more of an art book with a sparse narrative, so reading it isn't essential for plot but is highly recommended to appreciate the stunning, melancholic visuals that inspired the film.

author: Kazuo Ishiguro
keyCast: Jenna Ortega, Amy Adams, Simon Baker
notes: This is an adaptation of the poignant sci-fi novel from Nobel laureate Kazuo Ishiguro, exploring themes of love, humanity, and obsolescence through the eyes of an 'Artificial Friend'. The film is directed by Taika Waititi, a choice that has generated significant buzz, with audiences curious to see how his signature style will mesh with Ishiguro's subtle, melancholic prose. Jenna Ortega stars as Klara, the observant android, with Amy Adams as the mother of the sick child she is purchased for. Given the book's Booker Prize nomination and Ishiguro's literary status, this is a prestige project to watch. Reading the book first is highly recommended to fully absorb the nuances of Klara's unique and moving perspective.

bookTitle: The Last Thing He Told Me (Season 2)
author: Laura Dave
keyCast: Jennifer Garner, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, Angourie Rice
notes: Following the success of the initial limited series, Apple TV+ renewed the mystery-thriller for a second season, which will be based on the forthcoming sequel novel by author Laura Dave. The first season followed Hannah Hall (Garner) as she forged a relationship with her stepdaughter while searching for the truth about her husband's disappearance. The renewal was a major announcement, as it extends the story beyond the original source material, with Dave actively writing the sequel book alongside the show's development. Production is slated to begin in late 2026. Reading the first book (or watching Season 1) is essential to understanding the characters and the central mystery.

author: Cixin Liu
keyCast: Benedict Wong, Jess Hong, Eiza González, John Bradley, Liam Cunningham
notes: Netflix has confirmed that the adaptation of Cixin Liu's mind-bending sci-fi epic will continue, covering the second and third books, 'The Dark Forest' and 'Death's End'. Showrunners David Benioff, D.B. Weiss, and Alexander Woo will return to tackle the incredibly complex and ambitious concepts of the later books, including the 'dark forest' theory of the universe and deep-time cosmic warfare. The first season was a critical and ratings success, praised for making the dense physics accessible, and the next installments are expected to be even grander in scale. Reading the books is almost a prerequisite to fully appreciate the philosophical and scientific depth, especially 'The Dark Forest', which is a fan favorite.

bookTitle: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
notes: This highly anticipated adaptation of Taylor Jenkins Reid's blockbuster novel tells the story of a reclusive Old Hollywood movie icon who decides to give a final interview to an unknown magazine reporter. The book was a cultural phenomenon, and the film rights sparked a major bidding war, won by Netflix. Leslye Headland ('Russian Doll') is set to direct, but casting for the coveted lead role of Evelyn Hugo remains one of the most hotly debated topics among fans. The project is currently in the scripting and pre-production phase. Reading the book is an absolute must, as its clever narrative structure and shocking final twist are the core of its appeal.

bookTitle: A Court of Thorns and Roses
author: Sarah J. Maas
notes: Based on the wildly popular 'romantasy' book series, this show follows mortal huntress Feyre Archeron after she is dragged into the dangerous, magical realm of the Fae. The adaptation was announced with Ronald D. Moore ('Outlander') and author Sarah J. Maas herself attached, generating massive excitement from the book's enormous fanbase. However, the project has since faced development hurdles and creative shifts, with Moore reportedly no longer the showrunner, and it remains in the scripting stage with no casting news. Despite the delays, the hype is immense. Reading the first book is highly recommended to understand the intricate world-building and character relationships before the series premieres.

author: Rebecca Yarros
notes: Amazon is adapting the viral TikTok sensation and #1 bestseller 'Fourth Wing', a fantasy romance set at a brutal war college for dragon riders. The story follows Violet Sorrengail, who is forced by her mother, the commanding general, to join the dangerous riders' quadrant despite her frail body. Amazon acquired the rights to the entire Empyrean series, signaling a major franchise investment. The project is in the very early stages of development with author Rebecca Yarros serving as an executive producer, but no writer or showrunner has been officially attached yet. Given the book's explosive popularity, reading it beforehand is essential to join the massive online conversation and appreciate the hype.

author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
notes: This series will adapt the popular YA mystery novel where an ordinary teenage girl, Avery Kylie Grambs, inexplicably inherits a billionaire's entire fortune, much to the shock of his surviving family. The catch is that she must move into his sprawling mansion, filled with secret passages and puzzles, and live alongside his four brilliant and dangerous grandsons. Amazon is developing the project after it was previously in development as a film, opting for a series to better explore the book's intricate plot and sequels. The project is currently in the scriptwriting phase. The book is a fast, fun read full of riddles and romantic tension, and reading it first would enhance the viewing experience.

author: E. Lockhart
notes: Based on the bestselling and twisty YA novel, this series is being developed by Julie Plec ('The Vampire Diaries') and Carina Adly MacKenzie ('Roswell, New Mexico'). The story centers on the wealthy, seemingly perfect Sinclair family who summer on a private island, and the dark secret that shatters their lives. The book is famous for its unreliable narrator and a shocking twist ending that became a phenomenon on 'BookTok'. The project is in the early development stage, with scripts being written. To experience the full impact of the story's big reveal, it is absolutely essential to read the book before watching the series or getting spoiled.

author: Christopher Paolini
notes: Disney+ is developing a new adaptation of the classic YA fantasy novel 'Eragon', the first book in 'The Inheritance Cycle'. The story follows a poor farm boy who discovers a dragon egg, leading him on an epic quest to overthrow a tyrannical king. This new series aims to be a more faithful adaptation than the panned 2006 film, with author Christopher Paolini serving as a co-writer and executive producer, a fact that has greatly encouraged fans. The project is in the scripting and early pre-production phase, with a global casting search underway for the lead roles. Reading the book is a great way to dive into the rich world of Alagaësia before the show brings it to life.

author: J.K. Rowling
notes: Max has announced a decade-long series that will be a faithful, book-by-book adaptation of the seven 'Harry Potter' novels. The project promises to explore the Wizarding World with a depth and detail that the film series couldn't achieve, with each season dedicated to one book. J.K. Rowling is attached as an executive producer to ensure fidelity to her original material, a point of both excitement and controversy. The search for a showrunner and an entirely new cast of young actors is ongoing, making this one of the most high-profile projects in Hollywood. While most are familiar with the story, re-reading the books would be a great way to spot the details and subplots the new series aims to include.

author: Kristin Hannah
notes: This adaptation of Kristin Hannah's massively popular historical novel about two sisters struggling to survive in Nazi-occupied France has been in development for years. The film is notable because it is set to star real-life sisters Dakota and Elle Fanning, playing on-screen sisters for the first time. Directed by Mélanie Laurent, the project has faced numerous pandemic-related delays and has been repeatedly removed from and re-added to the release schedule. It is currently in post-production but without a firm release date. Reading the powerful and emotional novel is highly recommended to prepare for what is expected to be a heart-wrenching film.

author: C.S. Lewis
notes: Netflix acquired the rights to all seven books in C.S. Lewis's beloved fantasy series with the intention of building a new, interconnected cinematic universe. Greta Gerwig ('Barbie', 'Little Women') has been hired to write and direct at least two of the films, a move that has generated immense curiosity about her take on the classic material. The project is still in the early stages of script development and pre-production, with no casting or specific book order announced. Given Gerwig's unique directorial vision, this is one of the most intriguing adaptations in the works. Re-reading at least 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe' is a good primer for whatever her vision may hold.

author: Agustina Bazterrica
notes: This is an adaptation of the shocking and controversial Argentinian horror novel set in a world where a virus has made all animal meat poisonous, leading to the legalization of institutionalized cannibalism. The story follows a man who works at a human processing plant and secretly struggles with the morality of his work. The film is being developed by director Agustín Toscano and is expected to be a deeply unsettling piece of social commentary horror. The project is in the early script phase. This book is not for the faint of heart, but reading it first is crucial to prepare for the film's brutal themes and allegorical depth.

author: Brit Bennett
notes: HBO is developing a limited series based on Brit Bennett's critically acclaimed novel, which follows identical twin sisters who run away from their small, southern Black community at age sixteen. Their lives diverge dramatically when one sister chooses to live as a white woman, exploring themes of race, identity, and family secrets across several decades. The project is being produced by Issa Rae's company Hoorae Media, with Aziza Barnes and Jeremy O. Harris co-writing. It's currently in the script development stage. The book's rich character work and multi-generational narrative make it a must-read before the series airs.

author: Madeline Miller
notes: HBO is adapting Madeline Miller's bestselling novel, a feminist retelling of Greek mythology centered on the minor goddess Circe. The book reimagines her story, from her struggles with the gods of Olympus to her exile on a remote island where she hones her witchcraft and encounters famous mythological figures. The project was announced with writers Rick Jaffa and Amanda Silver ('Planet of the Apes') attached, but news has been sparse, suggesting a long development process. The book's lyrical prose and powerful character arc made it a modern classic, and reading it is essential to appreciate the depth the series will aim to capture.

author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
notes: Based on the bestselling horror-thriller, this limited series is in development from Kelly Ripa and Mark Consuelos's production company. The story follows a glamorous 1950s socialite from Mexico City who travels to a remote, decaying mansion in the countryside to check on her newly-married cousin, only to uncover terrifying secrets about the house and its strange inhabitants. Author Silvia Moreno-Garcia is attached as an executive producer. The project is in the early development and scripting phase. Reading the book first is highly recommended to savor its unique blend of gothic horror, historical fiction, and body horror.

author: Matt Haig
notes: This film will adapt Matt Haig's beloved international bestseller about Nora Seed, a woman who finds herself in a library between life and death with the chance to try out alternative lives she could have lived. The film rights were acquired by StudioCanal, with writer and director Gil Kenan ('A Boy Called Christmas') attached to the project. The adaptation aims to capture the book's heartwarming and life-affirming tone, exploring themes of regret and possibility. The project is in the scripting phase, with casting yet to be announced. The book is a quick and uplifting read, and its episodic structure should translate well to film, making it a good but not essential pre-read.

author: Blake Crouch
notes: Netflix is developing a feature film based on Blake Crouch's high-concept sci-fi thriller, as part of a larger deal with Shonda Rhimes's Shondaland and Matt Reeves's 6th & Idaho production company. The novel deals with 'False Memory Syndrome,' a mysterious affliction that drives its victims mad with memories of a life they never lived, and a neuroscientist who invents a technology that could be the cause. The project is in the script development phase, aiming to create a mind-bending cinematic universe alongside Crouch's other works. Reading the book is highly recommended to get a handle on its complex, time-bending plot before it hits the screen.

author: Stephenie Meyer
notes: Lionsgate Television is in early development on a TV series adaptation of Stephenie Meyer's massively popular 'Twilight' book series. The project is intended to be a new interpretation of the story of Bella Swan and the vampire Edward Cullen, separate from the blockbuster film franchise. Author Stephenie Meyer is expected to be involved in the adaptation, but few other details, including the creative team or whether it will be live-action or animated, have been confirmed. The announcement has sparked a mix of nostalgia and curiosity. A re-read of the books could be fun to compare and contrast the new series' take on the iconic characters and plot points.

bookTitle: The House in the Cerulean Sea
author: T.J. Klune
notes: Amazon is developing a series based on T.J. Klune's heartwarming fantasy
